hints.content:
$\displaystyle \lim_{x\to -6}f(x)$ represents the limit of $f$ as $x$ approaches $-6$.

We see that $f(-6)\approx -4$, but the $y$-values seem to approach a different value as the $x$-values approach $-6$.

![The graph of function f has arrows pointing along the curve, up to the right and down to the left, respectively, to the open circle.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/c16ab9206f601b45c0df9aebffcfc1264f010583)

The limit seems to be somewhere between $y=-6$ and $y=-5$, but slightly closer to $y=-6$.

![The graph of function f has a dashed horizontal line intersecting the open circle between y = negative 5 and y = negative 6, closer to y = negative 6.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/235cb87df9db5379d51d5344a33959819508ebe6)

question.content:
The function $f$ is defined for all real numbers.

![Function f is graphed. The x-axis goes from negative 8 to 8. The graph consists of a curve and a closed circle. The curve starts in quadrant 3 and moves upward through an open circle at x = negative 6, just above y = negative 6. The curve continues upward to quadrant 2, moves downward to quadrant 4, moves upward, and ends in quadrant 1. The closed circle is plotted at x = negative 6, just above y = negative 4.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/d984ae7b1dd842c610b97179be74d19d7ae45e96)

**What is a reasonable estimate for $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to -6}f(x)$ ?**
